name: Progression Gate
tagline: A standing requirement that withholds a defined part of the product until a progression measure the product itself advances reaches a stated value.
desc: A progression gate ties the availability of a defined part of the product, a feature, an area, a mode, an item, to a progression measure the product maintains and advances through the user's own activity, a level, a tier, a completion count. The condition exists as a standing state on the withheld part rather than only as a one-time event: it's observable before it's satisfied, and reaching the stated value changes availability under the product's own rule. The boundary that matters most is what kind of condition it is. Only a measure the product itself advances through use qualifies; jurisdiction, identity verification, purchase entitlements, and comparable eligibility conditions are a different thing entirely, they can't be satisfied simply by using the product, and this library assigns them no mechanic label at all.
principle: The condition stands whether or not it's ever crossed. What makes something a gate rather than ordinary sequence is that it's a stated requirement on a part distinct from the progression itself, not simply the next unit of it.
warn: The boundary against ordinary eligibility is this entry's weakest edge and worth checking deliberately: jurisdiction, identity verification, purchase entitlements, and account standing are conditions the user cannot satisfy simply by using the product, and none of them qualify, however similar the lock screen looks to one that does. The same care runs the other way: the very next level in an ordered sequence is the progression itself, not a separate part gated behind it, unless the product states some further requirement on top of just reaching it.
variants: Level gate, the requirement is a stated level, tier, or rank
Count gate, the requirement is a stated number of completed activities, items obtained, or events logged
Browsable gate, the withheld part can be opened, viewed, or explored before it becomes usable
Staggered gates, several related parts are gated at different values on the same measure, releasing them one at a time
Bypassable gate, the product offers a defined alternative route to the part alongside the measure
lifecycle: Needs a progression measure already in motion before there's anything to gate, so nothing is withheld until the measure exists. Most visible once a user is close enough to the stated value to see the withheld part as something specific to reach, rather than an abstract future feature.
